credits.source: KUAT SHIPWRIGHT / craft_tie_in (OKB2025), based on “Star Wars: TIE/in Interceptor” by Daniel
credits.changes: Adapted collector planform and hardware; rebuilt cockpit, arm assemblies, mounts and powerplant. Cockpit detail also adapted from the supplied TIE/D design. Avenger prototype: new split collector wings, heavy port battery, reinforced wing spars, six inboard launchers and enlarged aft hull. Avenger photo revision: split forward/aft blades, opposed armored and photovoltaic faces, forked rails, new wing yokes, armored canopy cheeks and recessed aft boarding hatch. Wingtip correction from marked hangar photograph: all sixteen light cannons on the four forward blades, with three along each leading edge and one beside the tip ranging optic. Shortened the aft central pod by 1.30 m, recontoured its two wing-root fairings, and repacked the engine bay. Reconstructed from the interrupted progress report supplied on 2026-11-24: central pod groups uniformly scaled to 87% about [3.06,3.51,0] (aft limit advanced 0.43693 m); full-size single-seat cockpit retained; wing front/rear projected reach set to 1.3:1 while retaining the hinge, root edges, and blade span. Interior packing and final game validation recorded separately. This reconstructs the reported stage, not recovered unsaved bytes. All 38 interior bodies retained their original dimensions and were repositioned using the game placement solver. Engine nozzles and machinery dimensions follow the 87% pod scale. Blade reach received a 10.7 mm overall-envelope correction, preserving the 1.3:1 front/rear ratio and fixed roots, to retain the 13.41 m installed overall length. Internal engine machinery restored to its original 0.64 m length and 0.31 m radius, shifted aft within the pod by adjusting the machinery offset to preserve propulsion efficiency; external nozzles retain the 87% scale. Reactor, cockpit, and all other internal bodies retain their original sizes. On 2026-11-25 the two internal drive housings were replaced by wider 0.615 m radius cylinders, the reactor was reduced to 1.50 m diameter, and four wing-root heat converters were retained. The single-seat cockpit, reactor and landing gear were repositioned internally. Drive feeds and hyperdrive length were matched to 4,500 G and Class 1. Six launcher mount flags and their routing were reconciled with the current game loader. Lightweight revision: the rear equipment bay now has a framed pressure hull inside its original outer plating. The 20 collector frames, spars and root joining plates now have closed air cells with internal webs. Both engine cores retain their full volume. Reactor diameter is 1.46 m, four wing-root heat converters are 0.63 m, and existing internal auxiliaries were sized to their supported loads. All hardpoints and the external nozzle assemblies retain their original locations. Photo-matched wing roots: tapered the upper and lower shoulders into both original reinforced shafts. Added an enclosed internal instrument mounting case and repacked the original targeting computer and structural integrity unit. Retuned the propulsion feeds and hyperdrive to the lighter airframe. Replaced the cheek-to-spar fairings and raised inboard collars with tapered shoulders meeting the native shaft profile. Removed the dorsal access hatch, knob, six windows and hull recess. Retained the aft boarding ramp. Repositioned the targeting computer and mounting case, inertial compensator, structural integrity unit and port landing gear. Added two internal engine beds inside the outer skin. Calibrated drive feeds and the hyperdrive for the final mass.
